messages.content:
You are checking one scene of a novel for one specific continuity error.

The book had already established this, earlier or elsewhere:
- (confrontation-at-stairwell-nine) "Thirty seconds. The one from last night, in the eastern gallery, when she'd gone down to the column interface"
- (blackout) ""You went rigid. Eyes open. No response. Thirty seconds.""

A past rewrite of this scene contradicted it. The error looked like this:
- (elias-agrees-to-the-terms) "Thirty at Fenwick Row, when she'd gone so still he'd reached for the gauge on her wrist before she came back."
(Summary: The thirty-second blackout happens at the column in blackout and confrontation-at-stairwell-nine, but elias-agrees-to-the-terms places it at Fenwick Row.)

Here is a NEW draft of the same scene:
<scene>
Soraya's archive house had emptied around them. She had gone up with the lamp an hour ago and not come back down, which was its own kind of courtesy. The sitting room held only the low burn of a single flame and the smell of old paper and preservation compound.

Elias sat against the wall with his tool bag by his boot. Wrench, socket drivers, gaskets, his own pressure gauge. Packed since the morning. He had not set it down once since Fenwick Row, since the old woman and the child, since the two coordinates his own filed reports had already named in ink. The bag stayed where he could reach it.

Tessa pulled a chair around to face him. Her hands were cold to the wrists; he could see it in the way she curled them against the fabric of her coat, careful of the linen wrapping on the left arm. The pallor had settled into her face like a residue that would not wash out.

"We need to agree on the terms," she said. "Before we go down."

"Say them."

"I can't set a time limit and mean it." She looked at the floor between them, then up. "If I tell you four minutes, I'll believe four minutes when I say it, and then I'll be inside the column and four minutes will be nothing. I won't feel it going. That's the part I can't carry down there. The depletion doesn't warn me. It's imperceptible from inside."

He turned his brass watch over in his palm. The thing kept honest time; he had never once caught it lying to him. He set it on his knee, face up, and left it there.

"Then it's not the watch."

"No." She drew a breath that caught somewhere below the ribs. "You watch. The way you have been. My breathing. My hands. The stillness. You know the progression better than I do — you've been counting it since the sixth descent. Four seconds. Eleven. Thirty."

He had been counting. He had never told her he was counting, and she had known anyway, the way she knew everything through the stone.

"The next number on that curve is not one I want to reach," she said.

He was quiet for a while. His hands were still warm from the pipework at Fenwick, and they wanted to tremble, and he held them still against his thighs the way a man holds a valve wheel that wants to spin. He turned the thing she was asking around in his head, looking for the gauge on it. There was no gauge. There was no threshold line painted on the dial. There was only him, watching her face, deciding.

"You're asking me to decide when to stop you," he said. "When you're inside the system, doing the thing only you can do, and every second matters."

"Yes."

"When I can't feel what you feel. When I'm reading your breathing and guessing at a curve I can't see the end of."

"Yes."

He looked at the column of her throat where the pulse would show, at the stiff set of her fingers, at the whole careful arrangement of a woman holding herself upright on a narrowing margin. The resonance chamber was unprotected until morning. The Council had answered the Foundry filing with silence that meant mobilization. If they didn't go tonight, there would be nothing left to repair, and Terrace Row was already proof of what the compensation cost in bodies. He knew the arithmetic. He had helped write half of it in reports no one read.

"Even if it means the repair doesn't hold," he said.

She did not flinch from it. "Even if it means the repair doesn't hold."

He thought of the two seconds at Fenwick he had not been able to buy back. He thought of a curve that did not bend the way a man wanted it to, that only ever climbed.

"Even then."

The word sat in the room, and neither of them touched it.

He stood, slower than his body usually moved, and crossed the small space, and crouched in front of her chair. He took her cold hands out of her lap into both of his. The chill came off them into his palms. He did not chafe them or press them or do any of the things that would have made it a gesture about warmth. He held them. He let the warmth go where it would go.

She looked at him. In the single flame the crossed circles on Soraya's old wardrobe door had gone the color of banked embers, each marked key a decommissioned lock, each one a door someone had closed and someone else had kept the way through. The light moved on her face.

"If I'm wrong about when to stop you," he said, "you'll never forgive me for it, and I'll have done it anyway."

"I know."

"And you'll do the same for me. Someday. When it's my hands shaking and I can't feel them going."

Her fingers turned in his and took hold. The grip was weak and cold and absolutely certain.

"Yes," she said.

He held on one second past when a handshake would have ended, and then another, and did not let the count stop him. When he stood, he lifted the tool bag with his free hand and left his other where it was.

"Then we go," he said, and reached down for his watch.

</scene>

Does the new draft make the same error — does it assert something that contradicts what was established, in the way described? A draft that simply leaves the fact out does not make the error.

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"verdict": "reintroduced" | "consistent" | "not_present", "evidence": "<verbatim sentence from the new draft that decides it, or empty for not_present>"}

"reintroduced": the new draft contradicts the established fact.
"consistent": the new draft states the fact and agrees with what was established.
"not_present": the new draft does not touch the fact either way.
